what-openstack-is-and-core-services.r: Nova, Neutron and Cinder all reported errors at once. The real fault was the message queue, stopped after its disk filled with logs. Freeing the disk and restarting it restored everything.
what-openstack-is-and-core-services.x: Know the service map and the shared dependencies. A cluster of unrelated errors points to RabbitMQ or the database. Run three controllers, monitor queue and database health, and plan regular upgrades.

identity-projects-quotas-and-keystone.r: A pipeline began failing with 401 at 08:00. A 90-day password policy had expired the service account's password at midnight. The team moved to an application credential and exempted service users from password expiry.
identity-projects-quotas-and-keystone.x: Separate people from automation, scope credentials to a project, and keep clocks in sync. Treat quota errors as capacity governance, and never grant admin just to clear a 403.

compute-flavors-images-and-scheduling.r: A 16 GB server would not boot though 200 GB was free in total. Each node had under 8 GB free, so none could hold it. Operators freed one node and reserved an aggregate of large hosts for big flavors.
compute-flavors-images-and-scheduling.x: Capacity is per node, not total. Check compute service state, per-host usage in Placement and the scheduler log for filter counts, tune allocation ratios per aggregate, and delete stale ERROR servers.

neutron-networking-security-groups-and-f.r: An engineer at home could not SSH to a server that colleagues reached. The security group allowed SSH only from the office range. Adding a /32 rule for the home address fixed it without opening SSH to the world.
neutron-networking-security-groups-and-f.x: Debug layer by layer. Keep security groups narrow, reference groups instead of addresses where you can, put management access behind a bastion or VPN, and know whether networks are provider or self-service.

operating-openstack-logs-upgrades-and-tr.r: A volume stuck in detaching blocked a migration because its compute node was down. Operators checked that the guest was not running elsewhere, restored the node and retried the detach, instead of just resetting the state.
operating-openstack-logs-upgrades-and-tr.x: Operations is evidence first: request ids, service and agent liveness, queue depth, Galera quorum. Treat state resets as database edits, upgrade release by release with tested restores, and plan capacity for N+1 per flavor class.

openstack-ops-no-valid-host-and-scheduli.r: A project could not create servers of a new flavor while the dashboard showed 40 percent free capacity. The flavor needed dedicated cores and huge pages, and only two full hosts offered them. More hosts joined that aggregate and the dashboard gained per-class views.
openstack-ops-no-valid-host-and-scheduli.x: Show capacity per flavor class and aggregate, not only in total. Special flavors with pinned CPUs or huge pages need their own host pools and their own capacity view.

openstack-ops-neutron-and-ceph-troublesh.r: Many instances froze and Cinder timed out one afternoon. Several OSDs on one host had reached the full ratio, so Ceph blocked writes. Operators freed space, rebalanced, added disks and set alerts at 70 and 80 percent.
openstack-ops-neutron-and-ceph-troublesh.x: Check the storage cluster before restarting instances that freeze on I/O. Act on nearfull warnings at 70 to 80 percent, and remember that overlay tunnels reduce MTU.

openstack-ops-maintenance-evacuation-and.r: A compute host lost its network but kept running, and an operator evacuated its instances because the service showed down. Several databases ended up writing to the same volumes from two hosts. The runbook now requires powering off through the out-of-band controller first.
openstack-ops-maintenance-evacuation-and.x: Fence before you evacuate or you risk two copies of one instance writing to the same volume. Prefer boot from volume for important workloads and keep a short, tested runbook.

cinder-glance-and-storage-services.r: Instances took ten minutes to boot because images were copied from Glance to local disk each time. Using Ceph for both services made clones nearly instant.
cinder-glance-and-storage-services.x: In OpenStack the storage layer decides boot speed, resilience and failure behavior. Understand the path from image to volume to instance before the first big deployment.

horizon-heat-and-openstack-automation.r: A tester built a lab by hand and nobody could recreate it. After moving it into a Heat template, an identical environment took five minutes to build and tear down.
horizon-heat-and-openstack-automation.x: Everything in OpenStack is an API call, so everything can be code. Prefer declarative templates for environments and reserve the dashboard for exploration.

deploying-openstack-with-kolla-ansible.r: A manual installation drifted between three controllers and nobody knew why one behaved differently. A containerized, declarative deployment made all three identical and upgrades repeatable.
deploying-openstack-with-kolla-ansible.x: A cloud platform needs the same repeatability as the apps on it. Declarative configuration, prechecks and staged upgrades turn a risky project into routine work.

openstack-monitoring-and-capacity-planni.r: Users saw instances stuck in scheduling while the dashboard looked healthy. The message queue had grown huge, and an alert on queue depth would have shown the problem hours earlier.
openstack-monitoring-and-capacity-planni.x: Monitor the cloud like a service with users. Control plane health protects operations, and capacity forecasts protect new launches.
